result.description:
MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Employment Type: Permanent Part Time
Position Classification: Midwifery Unit Manager Level 1
Remuneration: $72.62 - $72.62 per hour plus superannuation
Hours Per Week: 24
Requisition ID: REQ679168
Located in: Randwick, Sydney
Application Close: Sunday 2 August 2026

Where you'll be working

The Royal Hospital for Women is a multi-faceted tertiary referral and teaching hospital, internationally recognised as one of the world's leading centres for the care of mothers, babies, and women with benign gynaecological and gynae-oncology conditions. As the only stand-alone women's hospital in New South Wales, it offers unique opportunities for innovative clinical practice and is committed to delivering excellence in women's health care through both practice and ongoing research.

Part of the South Eastern Sydney Local Health District (SESLHD), the hospital is co-located with other major facilities on the Randwick Hospitals Campus-one of the State's most comprehensive health care precincts. This location supports a rich environment for collaboration and expertise across specialties.

Ideally situated between the University of New South Wales and Coogee Beach, The Royal Hospital for Women is just 15 minutes from Sydney's Central Business District and harbour. Its proximity to some of Sydney's best beaches, restaurants, and sporting facilities offers staff the added benefit of a vibrant lifestyle alongside a rewarding and supportive professional environment. 

The Role

The RHW Birthing Services include the areas of Birthing Unit, Birth Centre and the Maternal Assessment Unit. The Midwifery Unit Manager 1 (MUM) is a clinical MUM coordinator role and provides clinical leadership and day to day coordination of the Birthing Services at the Royal Hospital for Women (RHW) in collaboration with the MUM 3 who has overall management responsibility for Birthing Services. 

The MUM 1 is responsible for the daily clinical co-ordination of Birthing Services and, the triage categorisation of women admitted to the Birthing Unit. The MUM 1 assists the MUM 3 to lead, plan and evaluate the service. The MUM 1 will work collaboratively with the MUM 3 to effectively manage resources and ensure optimal patient outcomes by promoting best practice through support, allocation and supervision of staff on a day to day basis. 

The MUM 1, in partnership with the MUM 3 participates in the recruitment and performance development of staff. The Clinical MUM 1 is responsible to the MUM 3 and functions within the policies and procedures of the NSW Ministry of Health, SESLHD, RHW and the Maternity Division. 

The purpose of the MUM 1 for Birthing Services is to: - Direct, allocate and co-ordinate women's care;

Ensure the practice of midwifery care is safe and efficient, maintaining standards of care through continual audits and quality improvement initiatives.

Lead and co-ordinate the midwifery and multi-disciplinary care team at the unit level 

Develop consumer engagement and feedback to improve services to women 

Benefits:

Salary packaging optionsthat reduce your taxable income and increase your take-home pay! Up to $9K for living expenses and $2.6K meal & entertainment & Novated Leasing.

Discounted gym memberships with a Fitness Passport

Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for employees and family members.

Discounted Private Health Insurance.

Selection Criteria:

Current registration as a Registered Midwife with the Nursing & Midwifery Board of Australia

Relevant management experience, or a combination of study and work experience with a demonstrated commitment to professional development

A demonstrated knowledge and-or experience in the management and delivery of health care services

Proven ability in innovative clinical service delivery, harm minimisation and practice development

Effective interpersonal and communication skills that demonstrate the ability to engage, enable and manage teams

Proven ability to create and maintain a positive workplace culture and articulate and achieve a vision for midwifery services.

Recent clinical experience in Maternity Birthing Services

Need more information? 

1) Click here for the Position Description and SESLHD Expected Standards
2) Find out more about applying for this position

For role related queries or questions contact Prue Shipway on Prue.Shipway@health.nsw.gov.au

Our CORE Values are Collaboration, Openness, Respect and Empowerment and have been created by employees for employees and help define how we work and to inspire positive interactions in the workplace.

We embrace diversity as our strength and are committed to maintaining an inclusive and collaborative work environment. Our workplaces are welcoming and safe for all our employees, irrespective of their unique characteristics including age, ethnicity, cultural or spiritual background, gender identity, disability, education and social-economic status. Read about our Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging Strategy for more information.

Reasonable Adjustments

NSW Health recognises everyone is unique, and that you may require some adjustments to ensure you have the best opportunity to apply. If we can make some adjustments to the NSW Health recruitment-interview process, then please email SESLHD-Recruitment-RHW-Corporate@health.nsw.gov.au and let us know.

Adjustments may include but are not limited to, physical requirements, interview setups and specific interview availability times where required.

Information for applicants:

An eligibility list may be created for future vacancies

If you have relevant qualifications or experience, please include any supporting documents with your application.

Employment of a temporary visa holder may only occur if no suitable permanent resident or citizen of Australia has been identified for this position following suitable labour market testing.

Applicants will be assessed against the essential requirements and selection criteria contained within the position description

Recommended applicants will be reviewed for compliance with NSW Health policy directive Occupational Assessment, Screening and Vaccination against Specific Diseases for all positions prior to offer

SESLHD is committed to creating a workplace that reflects the diversity of our community. This will help ensure our employees, our patients and their carers, feel supported. We invite candidates of all ages, genders, sexual orientation, cultural background, people with disability, neurodiverse individuals, and Indigenous Australians to apply. We do have an Aboriginal Workforce Team that can also provide support (SESLHD-AboriginalWorkforce@health.nsw.gov.au) and for additional information please visit our Stepping Up Website

Target Business Services

Location: 91-109 Main Neerim Road, Neerim South, Victoria 3831
Salary: $80,000 plus 12% superannuation
Position: Full time, Permanent

Our client, AFS Consulting Group Pty. Ltd. trading as Neerim South Hotel, is a well-established hospitality venue located in the heart of Neerim South, Victoria. The hotel offers quality accommodation, a popular bistro, bar facilities, and function spaces, providing a welcoming destination for both local patrons and visitors. The business is committed to delivering high standards of customer service, quality dining, and memorable guest experiences.

The business is seeking to appoint an experienced Hotel Manager to oversee the day-to-day operations of the hotel, ensuring efficient service delivery across accommodation, food and beverage, and front-of-house operations. The primary purpose of this role is to manage operational performance, lead the hospitality team, maintain compliance with industry regulations, and contribute to the hotel's continued commercial success.

This role is integral to maintaining the hotel's reputation for quality hospitality while driving operational efficiency, customer satisfaction, and business growth.

Minimum Requirements:

-	Diploma or equivalent qualification as recognised under the Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF). A qualification in Hospitality Management, Business, or a related discipline is highly desirable.
-	Minimum one year of relevant experience in a similar management role within the hospitality industry.

Key Responsibilities:

-	Oversee the daily operations of the hotel, including accommodation, bar, bistro, functions, and customer service activities.
-	Monitor operational performance to ensure high standards of guest service, cleanliness, and presentation are consistently maintained.
-	Recruit, supervise, train, and evaluate staff while fostering a productive and customer-focused workplace culture.
-	Manage guest enquiries, complaints, and service issues promptly to ensure high levels of customer satisfaction.
-	Prepare budgets, monitor financial performance, control operating costs, and provide regular reports to the Director.
-	Ensure compliance with liquor licensing, food safety, workplace health and safety, and all relevant regulatory requirements.
-	Coordinate maintenance programs and liaise with contractors to ensure hotel facilities remain safe and well maintained.
-	Manage purchasing, inventory, and supplier relationships to maintain efficient stock control and cost-effective operations.
-	Develop and implement promotional initiatives, functions, and local marketing activities to increase patronage and revenue.
-	Monitor customer feedback and implement continuous improvements to enhance operational performance and guest experience.

Skills and Experience:

-	Demonstrated leadership and team management skills within a hospitality environment.
-	Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with a strong customer service focus.
-	Sound financial management skills, including budgeting, cost control, and performance reporting.
-	Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities in a fast-paced operational environment.
-	Excellent organisational and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple operational functions.
-	Knowledge of hospitality operations, food and beverage service, accommodation management, and venue promotions.
-	Thorough understanding of relevant hospitality legislation, including liquor licensing, food safety, workplace health and safety, and employment obligations.

To apply, please send your resume to recruitment@targetbusiness.com.au
Please note: Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. All applications will be treated in the strictest confidence.

Location: Darwin NT
Employment Type: Full-time
Hours: 38 hours per week, Monday to Friday
Salary: AUD $67,510 – $75,000 per annum plus superannuation, depending on skills and experience

About Us
Skills and Hands NT Pty Ltd is a Northern Territory-based consultancy focused on workforce planning, talent engagement, and sustainable staffing strategies. We work alongside local businesses to support the development of strong, reliable teams through tailored pathways that align with their long-term goals. Our role is to facilitate practical workforce solutions that help employers attract and retain skilled talent—contributing to the resilience and continuity of operations across the Territory.

About the Employer
The business (ABN 53 603 812 004) is a Darwin-based professional cleaning business servicing commercial, industrial and government clients across the Northern Territory. We provide duct cleaning, air-conditioning cleaning and maintenance, kitchen exhaust cleaning, cool room cleaning, mould remediation, inspection reporting and cleaning schedules.
We are looking for a General Clerk to support our office, administration and customer service functions.

About the Role
The General Clerk will perform general clerical and administrative duties to support daily business operations. The role will assist with customer enquiries, job records, technician paperwork, service reports, filing, data entry and general office support.

The successful applicant will:
- Record, prepare, sort, classify and file customer, supplier and job information.
- Maintain digital and paper records for cleaning, HVAC, duct, mould and maintenance jobs.
- Answer telephone calls, emails and customer enquiries.
- Provide customers with basic information about services, bookings and job documentation.
- Prepare routine documents, job records, service reports and internal summaries.
- Enter customer details, job information and technician notes into business systems.
- Proofread and correct routine emails, forms, reports and service documents.
- Assist with scheduling records, site access paperwork and technician job paperwork.
- Scan, copy, upload and file documents, photos and completion evidence.
- Sort incoming and outgoing mail and office documents.
- Assist with reception duties and general office administration.
- Maintain confidentiality of customer, staff and business records.

Applicants should have:
- Experience in clerical, office administration, reception, customer service or data entry work.
- Good computer skills, including email, Microsoft Office or similar systems.
- Good attention to detail and accurate data entry skills.
- Ability to organise records and manage routine paperwork.
- Clear communication skills.
- Ability to work with customers, technicians, suppliers and management.
- Ability to manage several administrative tasks at the same time.

Applicants should have:
- Certificate II or III in Business, Business Administration or a related field; or
- At least 1 year of relevant clerical or administrative experience.

How to Apply
We are looking for a reliable and organised administration professional who can support our office operations, maintain accurate records, assist with customer enquiries, and help keep our cleaning and maintenance jobs running smoothly.

To apply, submit the following:
- Resume outlining your work experience and references.
- A short cover letter (max. 300 words) explaining:
- Why you are applying for this position; and
- An example of when you showed excellent service, initiative, or teamwork (use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, Result).
- A Written Response (max. 600 words) describing how your skills and experience align with the responsibilities of the role you are applying for. Please structure your example(s) using the STAR method.

* Only complete applications that address all three components will be considered. Incomplete or generic submissions will not be shortlisted.
If you are interested in joining a practical, professional team that delivers specialist HVAC, duct, exhaust, mould and commercial cleaning services across the Northern Territory, we look forward to receiving your application.

Apply online only. Walk-in or telephone enquiries regarding this vacancy will not be accepted.

Applications close: 1 August 2026

Customer Service Officers | Government Opportunities 
 Randstad is currently recruiting Customer Service Officers for well-known and reputable Government Departments. These opportunities are ideal for people-oriented professionals who thrive in dynamic environments and are looking to contribute to essential public services. 
 Assignments of up to 3 months are available with a high view for extension. Work days are Monday to Friday, with full-time hours scheduled between 8am and 5.30pm. The hourly rate for these positions is $37 - $40 plus super. 
 The Role 
 As a Customer Service Officer, you will provide high-level advisory and administrative support. You will be a primary point of contact, ensuring that queries are resolved efficiently and departmental records are kept up to date. 
 Key Responsibilities: 
 
 
 Provide high-level advisory and issue resolution for diverse customers. 
 
 
 Offer guidance to queries and interpret complex customer information. 
 
 
 Perform high-level administrative tasks and generate appropriate documentation. 
 
 
 Maintain records management processes, including regular updates and reviews. 
 
 
 Manage high-volume inquiries both face-to-face and over the phone. 
 
 
 About You 
 We are looking for adaptable professionals with a strong background in customer service, reception, or administration. To be successful in this role, you will have: 
 
 
 Highly developed verbal and written communication skills. 
 
 
 Experience in dealing with high-volume calls and a professional phone manner. 
 
 
 Sound knowledge of the Microsoft Windows PC environment and strong Microsoft Office skills. 
 
 
 Strong alpha and numerical data entry skills with high attention to detail. 
 
 
 The ability to problem solve and learn new technologies quickly. 
 
 
 Mandatory Compliance: You must hold a current National Police Clearance (NPC). This is a mandatory requirement. A Working with Children Check (WWCC) is highly ideal but not essential for all roles. 
 
 
 Why Work for Randstad? 
 Join Randstad's community of contractors and enjoy a range of benefits designed to support your career: 
 
 
 Three pay runs per week to ensure you are paid within the week. 
 
 
 Access to the My Randstad portal for easy payslip access. 
 
 
 Exclusive access to roles before they go to market. 
 
 
 Discounts at major retailers like David Jones, Myer, JB Hi-Fi, Woolworths, and more. 
 
 
 Access to our employee assistance program, including confidential counseling services. 
 
 
 A genuine support team dedicated to your development and success. 
 
 
 How to Apply

Job Description:

We are looking for a special kind of person - a St Vincent's kind of person. Someone who puts compassion, connection and caring for other people at the heart of everything they do.

As a Food Services Assistant, you'll be part of an experienced, engaged and dedicated team helping to create a welcoming, professional and supportive care experience for the residents of our Eltham facility.

St Vincent's Care, Eltham is just 20 kilometres north-east of Melbourne's city centre and is well known for its vast amount of green space. We provide a welcoming and inclusive community where our residents enjoy the comfort of a relaxed lifestyle. 

What's on your CV is important, but what's in your heart matters more, because at St Vincent's, kindness works for us.

Two Permanent Part Time positions are available with shifts across morning (AM) and afternoon (PM) during weekdays. 

Strong weekday availability is essential. 

Things that work for us:

An ability to provide a catering and kitchen service that is consistent with the mission and philosophy of our organisation

Experience in hospitality, an aged care facility, hospital environment and-or related field ideal

Providing services that support high quality food services outcomes for residents, customers and staff of the Facility

Ability to work a rotating roster, flexible

High level of customer service skills

Strong attention to detail and excellent communication skills

Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check

NDIS Worker Screening Check may be a requirement of this role.

Things that work for you:

Competitive salary packaging options up to $15,990, Novated leasing, plus an optional Meals and Entertainment card up to $2,650 per annum

Opportunity to work for the nation's largest Catholic not-for-profit health and aged care provider, with a rapidly growing and progressive vision

Friendly team environment with a great community care spirit

Ability to visibly see your impact on the business and its service

No cost uniforms and training

Free annual flu vaccination

Employee Assistance Program for staff and their families

Access to the Fitness Passport (FP)
 

Why become part of the St Vincent's Care family?

Because you're like us, you believe that every act of kindness makes the world a better place. Better for everyone who lives in the 20+ facilities and locations we operate in Queensland, New South Wales and Victoria. Better for all our staff and employees, who work tirelessly to provide the highest levels of care and quality of life for our clients. And better support for the local communities we play an important role in and continue to support.

At St Vincent's we value inclusivity and diversity and acknowledge the important of creating a work environment that is welcome, safe, fair and impartial and invite people from all backgrounds to join our caring family.
